solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Order check on empty surgery

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its shell, the first and last letters

parts.note: to stem is to check, as a flow of blood

explanation.surface: A hospital with no patients is told to tighten things up.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'A on B' puts B first, so the check comes after the emptied surgery. The medical surface makes 'check' sound like an examination.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both name an organised, methodical arrangement, as in 'law and order' against 'a filing method'.

clue.text: Judges thus arresting conservative thinker

indicators.note: to arrest is to seize and hold

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Judges detain a right-wing intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judges' opens the clue but its letters close the answer; 'thus' goes in front, and the pair together hold the Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Athenian philosopher is the archetypal thinker.

clue.text: Husband trapped by waters beginning to rise is cut off

indicators.note: a beginning is the first part, so only the first letter of 'rise' is used
something trapped is enclosed

explanation.surface: A husband caught in rising floodwater is stranded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut off' looks like the stranding of the surface, but it is a verb: to clip away.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to clip wool from a sheep or a branch from a tree is to cut it off.

clue.text: Wingless Madagascan creature — it can't fly

indicators.note: a word's wings are its two outer letters, so they are removed

explanation.surface: A zoology note about a flightless animal from Madagascar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wingless' fits the surface as a description of a bird, but it is the instruction that clips the lemur at both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the big Australian bird is flightless.

clue.text: Extremely clever, my boss — I owe him

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the person owed

indicators.note: takes the extremes, the first and last letters, of 'clever'

parts.note: a newspaper setter's boss runs the paper

explanation.surface: A crossword setter flatters the boss to whom they are in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter speaks as themselves: 'my boss' is the person in charge of the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the person a debtor owes money to.

clue.text: Correct groom once again

definitions.meaning: a verb: to put right a wrong
groom = dress, once again = RE, so a split word

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy someone up a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word: RE (again) plus DRESS (groom).
explanation.definitionFit: First sense a plain synonym, to remedy a grievance; second sense literal, dressing someone a second time.

clue.text: Sensible review of time on death row?

indicators.note: a review goes over the letters again, putting them in a new order

explanation.surface: A sober look back at years spent awaiting execution.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a prisoner's memoir; 'time' contributes only its abbreviation to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone with their feet on the ground is practical and realistic.

clue.text: Last of atheist philosopher's articles for union

indicators.note: takes the final letter of 'atheist'

explanation.surface: An atheist philosopher's last writings on political union.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s reads as a possessive but means 'is', joining wordplay to definition; the union is a marriage, not a political one.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the clothes and linen a bride gathers for her marriage.

clue.text: Turn down official employment

parts.note: a ref (referee) is a sports official
use = employment, as of a tool

explanation.surface: Someone declines a government job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Official employment' looks like a civil-service job; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to decline an offer.

clue.text: Setting for Oedipus Rex film announced

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken, so the word is heard, not seen

explanation.surface: A cinema listing names the location of a Sophocles tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' tempts toward a screen version of Oedipus; it is the John Travolta musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Sophocles set the tragedy in Thebes, a city of the ancient Hellenic world.

clue.text: Eventful game for the most part, with English heading for defeat

indicators.note: most of the word, so the last letter goes

parts.note: CHEQUERS, the board game, minus its last letter

indicators.note: the head, first letter, of 'defeat'

explanation.surface: A sports report: England lose a lively match.
explanation.walkthrough: Chequers is the British name for checkers (draughts).
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a history of mixed fortunes, ups and downs, is called this, like a board of light and dark squares.

clue.text: Move back to accommodate old novelist

indicators.note: to move back is to go the other way, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone retreats to make room for an elderly author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move back' reads as one phrase, but 'back' is the reversal of a single word for move.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Virginia, author of Mrs Dalloway, is a famous English writer of fiction.

clue.text: Contraction initially impacting German debt adversely

indicators.note: the letters are treated badly, knocked into a new order
takes the first letter of 'impacting'

explanation.surface: An economic shrinkage first hitting Germany's debt badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The economics surface makes 'Contraction' a recession; here it means a shortening.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a shortened version of a text is a contraction of it.

clue.text: Two kisses signifying a betrayal?

definitions.meaning: a kiss at the end of a letter is written X, so two kisses are XX
treachery against someone who trusted you

explanation.surface: Two kisses as the sign of a traitor, as Judas's kiss was.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Judas betraying Jesus with a kiss; the first sense is literal, XX being a pair of the letter-writer's crosses.
explanation.definitionFit: First sense literal, XX; second sense an idiom for cheating an ally.

clue.text: Close relation lives on benefits in the end

indicators.note: takes the last letter of 'benefits'

explanation.surface: A family member ends up living on welfare.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'A on B' puts B first, so the end of 'benefits' comes before 'lives'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal abbreviation of sister, a close family relation.

clue.text: Reporter's in contact with source on the way from France

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the words, so we hear them

parts.note: on = in contact with, root = source

explanation.surface: A journalist, travelling from France, reaches a contact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From France' belongs to the definition: the phrase is borrowed from French.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed French phrase meaning on the way, used as is in English.

clue.text: Facts about island's earliest broadcast

indicators.note: letters broadcast are scattered like seed

explanation.surface: A report on the first programme transmitted from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the radio surface; here it scatters the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: things as they actually are.

clue.text: Nation somehow "discontented", PM concludes

indicators.note: to conclude is to come last, so the PM goes at the end
read as dis-content-ed: the word 'somehow' has its content, its middle, removed

explanation.surface: A country somehow unhappy as its prime minister wraps up.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks show 'discontented' is to be taken literally, not as unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a Scandinavian country.

clue.text: A hothead, one sadly falling abroad

parts.note: a drop that falls from the eye when one is sad

explanation.surface: A reckless youth, one who falls on hard times overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One sadly falling' reads as a person's downfall; it is a teardrop.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal word for a reckless, unruly young person, a hothead.

clue.text: Republican party winning everything in race

indicators.note: to win something is to take it into your possession

parts.note: the GOP (Grand Old Party) is the US Republican Party

explanation.surface: An election report: the Republicans sweep the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' looks like the election; it is the definition, a fast run.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a horse's fastest pace, and a fast run, as in 'race along'.

clue.text: Pressure on television channel to be in charge

parts.note: old British slang for a TV channel, as in 'switch over to the other side'

explanation.surface: Lobbying a TV station to take control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is not positional here but its own piece, meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to chair a meeting or court is to be in charge of it.

clue.text: Millions in favour of trade union backing case for election

indicators.note: going backwards, so the outer letters that follow are read in reverse
a case is the outside, so take the outer letters of 'election'

parts.note: outer letters of election, turned round

explanation.surface: A union supporting an election campaign stands to gain millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reads as the union's support; it turns round the case of 'election'.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a vast sum of money, such as millions.

clue.text: Boozy capacity of female briefly irritating

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A woman's drinking habits are getting on someone's nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an old British beer-cask measure, a quarter of a barrel, which is why 'capacity' is boozy.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-friendly old unit: a small cask holding nine gallons of ale.

clue.text: Panic-stricken broadcast drops middle section

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so the central letters are lost

explanation.surface: A radio programme in a panic cuts its central segment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' is not radio here but sowing, as a farmer throws seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: frightened.

clue.text: Character seen in first part of book?

parts.note: CH = chapter, a part of a book

explanation.surface: Where a character first appears in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person in a story; it is a letter, and the first part of a book is Chapter One.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword sense: a character is a letter, here the Greek letter written X.

clue.text: Resolve differences: exonerate sole successor in hearing

parts.note: to exonerate someone is to declare them innocent

indicators.note: the phrase is taken as heard

parts.note: the only successor is THE heir

explanation.surface: A family feud settled when the only heir is cleared at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' suggests a court case, fitting 'exonerate'; it signals the sound of the heir.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to dispel tension by talking things through.

clue.text: Make modifications to 'arness

indicators.note: the apostrophe marks a dropped H, so the synonym also loses its H

parts.note: harness = HALTER, spoken with a dropped H in Cockney style

explanation.surface: A request to adjust some tack for a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'arness tells you to drop the H of its synonym too, as a Cockney would.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to change.

clue.text: African native being ironic, you say? I disagree

indicators.note: tells you to go by the sound

explanation.surface: An argument over whether an African's remark was sarcastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African native' suggests a person; it is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the big horned animal lives wild in Africa.

clue.text: Dish his wife tries out

indicators.note: the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A man's wife experiments with a new recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen surface hides that 'wife' contributes only W.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a mutton, potato and onion stew.

clue.text: Fringe uninspiring? On the contrary

indicators.note: the relation runs the other way: uninspiring is the answer backwards, so reverse it

parts.note: meh is slang for dull, uninspiring

explanation.surface: Someone finds a fringe unimpressive, then thinks better of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'Fringe reversed is uninspiring'; 'on the contrary' says the reversal goes the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the edge of a garment.

clue.text: Underworld boss losing millions in stock exchange crash perhaps

indicators.note: to lose something is to be without it, so the M for millions is removed

explanation.surface: A gangster loses millions in a market crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld boss' reads as a crime lord, but the words split: the classical underworld, then a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a market crash is one kind of calamity, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Obsequious southern host entertaining maiden

parts.note: a host is an army, as in heavenly host
M = maiden, a cricket over with no runs

explanation.surface: A fawning Southern host charms a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' suggests someone entertaining guests; it is a multitude of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: oily and ingratiating.
